en: Udāna 4.10 Sāriputtaupasamasutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion the Venerable Sāriputta was sitting not far from the Blessed One, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and reviewing his own tranquility.
The Blessed One saw the Venerable Sāriputta sitting not far away, having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and reviewing his own tranquility.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“For the bhikkhu whose mind is perfectly tranquil, whose guide has been severed;”
The wandering through births is exhausted;
he is liberated from the bonds of Māra. Thus ends the tenth [discourse].
The Yakkha with the Nāga as the fifth;
Upasena Vaṅgantaputta and Sāriputta— these ten.
